title: Leg Pain
correct_orders: Compression US (if high Wells or + D-dimer)
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with unilateral leg swelling, pain, warmth, and erythema. Risk factors: Virchow's triad — stasis (immobilization, long travel), hypercoagulability (malignancy, OCPs, pregnancy, thrombophilia), endothelial injury (surgery, trauma). Exam: Homan's sign unreliable. Measure leg circumference difference. Wells criteria determines pretest probability. If low probability → D-dimer. If D-dimer elevated or high probability → compression ultrasound (proximal DVT). Treatment: most DVT → anticoagulation with DOAC (rivaroxaban, apixaban) or LMWH bridge to warfarin. Duration: provoked = 3 months, unprovoked = 6-12 months or indefinite. NO routine thrombectomy or IVC filter unless anticoagulation contraindicated. Compression stockings for symptom relief and post-thrombotic syndrome prevention.
